name: @ploa/cli

tools.name: ploa_setup_guide
tools.description: Start here for a new app, or when the stores or Ploa aren't set up yet. Works out where this folder stands (signed in, app IDs in the Expo config, linked to Ploa, each store connected, the app created in each store, signing, store page, first build) and returns what's next, in order: who does each step (the person or you), what to do, and the exact links in App Store Connect, Play Console, Google Cloud and Ploa. When the app has no bundle ID or package name yet, suggests a few to choose from and explains how the stores treat them. Read-only; run it again after each step.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_link
tools.description: Links the Expo app in this folder to Ploa, like `ploa init`: finds the app in Ploa by its bundle ID or package name, or adds it with the workspace's App Store and Google Play connections, and writes ploa.json (the app's Ploa ID and server, no secrets; fine to commit). Needs ios.bundleIdentifier or android.package in the Expo config. With several connections for a store, name one with apple or google.

apple.description: The App Store connection's name, when there are several.

google.description: The Google Play connection's name, when there are several.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_preflight
tools.description: Checks this Expo / React Native app for what App Store Connect and Google Play would reject, before spending time on a build: version and build numbers against the stores, bundle IDs, the icon, iOS purpose strings, privacy manifest, export compliance, Play's target SDK, sensitive permissions, and secrets committed to git. Returns each finding with how to fix it.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_access
tools.description: Who this Ploa token belongs to and what it may do: its access level (read, draft, submit, production), and whether its owner made it autonomous, in which case App Review, production, prices, testers and products go straight through instead of waiting for a person's approval.

tools.name: ploa_status
tools.description: Shows what App Store Connect and Google Play have for this app right now: recent iOS builds and their processing state, App Store versions, and Google Play tracks with their releases and rollout.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_release_start
tools.description: Builds the app and sends it to testers: iOS to TestFlight (signed with the certificate Ploa issues for this build), Android to Google Play internal testing (Ploa signs it with the upload key it keeps). By default it builds on this machine; where: "github" builds on GitHub instead, from the commit on the app's release branch (or sha), with the workflow Ploa wrote for the repo (the app's GitHub card in Ploa sets it up): Android on GitHub's Linux runners, iOS only on the person's own Mac registered as a self-hosted runner with the label ploa (it waits for that runner). It builds what's committed and pushed, not local changes. It runs in the background, since a build takes minutes and Apple's processing up to half an hour, and returns a release ID right away; follow it with ploa_release_status. The build number is the next free one unless you pass one. Run ploa_preflight first. This never goes to App Review or production: those need ploa_release_submit_review or ploa_release_promote, and a person's approval.

buildNumber.description: iOS build number or Android versionCode. Default "auto": one higher than anything the store has. On GitHub always "auto".

where.description: Where to build: "here" (this machine, the default) or "github" (from what is pushed; iOS on the person's self-hosted Mac runner).

sha.description: On GitHub: the commit to build. Default: the head of the app's release branch.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_release_status
tools.description: Where a release stands: building, uploading, being processed by Apple, on TestFlight or internal testing, or failed and why. While it builds on this machine, includes the last lines of the build log.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

tools.name: ploa_release_changes
tools.description: The pull requests merged and the commits between two releases, from the app's GitHub repo (linked on its GitHub card in Ploa): for a release, since the release of its platform before it; with no release, what the release branch has had since the live version (or else the last release that reached testers). Each PR comes with its title, author and description. Use it to write release notes from what people did rather than commit messages alone (the write_release_notes prompt).

releaseId.description: A release. Left out: the app's release branch since the live version.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_release_submit_review
tools.description: Asks a person to approve submitting an iOS build that is on TestFlight for App Review; the in-app products that are ready to submit go to review with it. When the version is already with App Review with an older build, this is refused and says so; replace: true then asks for both steps under one approval: Ploa withdraws the version from App Review, puts this build on it and submits it (App Review starts over). Nothing is sent to Apple until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard; this returns at once with the request's ID, so check it with ploa_approval_status. Needs a token allowed to submit.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

replace.description: The version is with App Review with another build: withdraw it and submit this build in its place, under one approval.

tools.name: ploa_release_withdraw_review
tools.description: Asks a person to approve taking an iOS version out of App Review (App Store Connect's Remove from review): Ploa cancels its review submission and waits until Apple shows the version as Developer Rejected, editable again, with its build still on TestFlight. Pass the release of any build of that version. To send a newer build in its place in one step, use ploa_release_submit_review with replace: true instead. Nothing changes at Apple until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard; check it with ploa_approval_status. Needs a token allowed to submit.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

tools.name: ploa_release_promote
tools.description: Asks a person to approve moving an Android release from internal testing to production (or beta / alpha), optionally as a staged rollout to a percentage of users. Nothing changes on Google Play until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard; this returns at once with the request's ID, so check it with ploa_approval_status. Needs a token allowed to touch production.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

rolloutPercent.description: Share of users for a staged rollout, 1 to 100. Default 100.

tools.name: ploa_runs
tools.description: Lists this app's recent release runs, newest first: each release Ploa carried (started from the CLI, an agent or the dashboard) with its state, who started it, when, how long it took to reach TestFlight or internal testing, the commit, and every step with its duration (build, upload, App Store Connect or signing, Apple processing or Google Play, the testing track, and the App Review or promotion step a person approves). Use it to see why a release failed or where it is.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_shipping_report
tools.description: One report of where this app stands everywhere, like the dashboard's Shipping page: the newest TestFlight build and App Store version, Google Play's testing and production tracks with the rollout, what waits for a person's approval, and the last release run. Read-only. Start here when asked how the app is doing or what to do next.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of using recent copies.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_quality
tools.description: How stable the app's released versions are, from the stores themselves. Read-only. Google Play: the user-perceived crash and ANR rates over 28 days, overall and per version code, against Play's bad-behavior thresholds (1.09% crashes, 0.47% ANRs), and the crashes and ANRs people hit most. App Store: Apple's API has no crash rates, so it gives what Apple offers: Xcode's performance metrics per version (launch time, hangs, memory, disk writes…) with Apple's regressions, and each build's diagnostics (hangs, disk writes, launches). Give releaseId (or platform and version) to check one release before promoting it or widening its rollout; leave them out for the whole app.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

version.description: Android: the version code. iOS: the build number.

versionName.description: iOS: the version the build belongs to, like 1.2.0.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of the copy from the last half hour.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_appstore_price_points
tools.description: Every price Apple offers in the app's base territory, cheapest first (0 is free), each with the pricePointId that ploa_details_save takes for step price.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_appstore_register_bundle_id
tools.description: For a new app: registers its iOS bundle ID with Apple (nothing happens if it's already there), so the person only picks it when creating the app in App Store Connect, which only a person can do there. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_android_upload_key_get
tools.description: Whether Ploa holds this app's Android upload key, the key every Android build is signed with before it goes to Google Play: its alias, SHA-256 fingerprint and expiry, and its certificate (public) as PEM. The key itself never leaves Ploa. Pass certificatePath to save the certificate there, for a person to give Play Console when it asks for one (Test and release › App integrity › Upload key › Request upload key reset).

certificatePath.description: Absolute path to save the certificate (.pem) to. Optional.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_android_upload_key_save
tools.description: Gives Ploa this app's Android upload key, which it keeps in its vault and signs every Android build with; it never leaves Ploa. how create: Ploa makes a new key (RSA 2048, valid 30 years) right in the vault, so no one holds a copy and no password passes through you. Use it only when Google Play has no upload key for this app yet (a new app, or one never uploaded): Play takes the first build's key as the upload key. how upload: an existing keystore (.keystore, .jks or .p12 in PKCS#12 format) from an absolute path on this machine, with its password and, if it holds several keys, the alias. Use it when Play already knows an upload key, for example one EAS or Android Studio made; take the password from the person or where they keep it, never write it into a file. A key Ploa already holds is replaced only with replace: true, and only when the person asked for it, since Play rejects builds signed with a key it doesn't know. Only a person, or an agent its owner made autonomous (see ploa_access), may do this; the workspace's owners are told each time.

path.description: how upload: absolute path to the keystore.

alias.description: how upload: the key's alias, if the keystore holds several.

replace.description: Replace the upload key Ploa already holds. Only when the person asked.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_product_get
tools.description: One in-app product or subscription as its store has it: kind, state, name and description per language, the US price, a subscription's period and free trial, on the App Store its subscription group, review note, Family Sharing and image (the one the App Store shows with it: url, Apple's state; Google Play keeps none), and under review what the store still needs before it can go to people and the next step (submit or activate). platform is ios or android; a Google Play subscription's productId is "product:basePlan", as the purchases list shows it. With no productId, what a new one needs: the store's primary language, the languages it takes, and the App Store's subscription groups.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_product_save
tools.description: Creates an in-app product or subscription in one store (leave productId out and put it in values), or changes one, straight to the store (needs a token allowed to submit). values: kind (subscription, consumable, non_consumable; on create), productId (on create: Apple takes letters, numbers, periods, underscores; Play lowercase), price (US dollars such as "4.99": Apple picks its nearest price point at or above, Play converts it for every country), period (subscriptions: P1W P1M P2M P3M P6M P1Y), trial (P3D P1W P2W P1M, or null to remove), listings ({ locale: { name, description } } in the store's own codes; Hebrew is "he" at Apple, "iw-IL" at Play; Apple names take 35 characters and descriptions 55, Play 55 and 200), and on the App Store referenceName, group (an existing group ID from ploa_product_get) or groupName (a new group), reviewNote, familySharable; on Play basePlanId. From an agent, a new product, a price or a free trial waits for a person's approval, since it sets what people pay; names and notes go straight through. An App Store subscription's price or free trial is set country by country and takes a few minutes: it answers with a job, which ploa_product_job follows.

productId.description: The product to change; leave out to create.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_product_job
tools.description: How far a long product write got (an App Store subscription's price, free trial or introductory offer, set country by country): its step (prices, trial_remove, trial, intro_remove, intro), how many of how many countries are done, and at the end what the store has now, or why it failed. Ask again every 20 seconds or so until state is done or failed.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_product_submit
tools.description: Sends one product on its way to people: on the App Store to App Review (Apple takes an app's first products only with a version; then it goes when the version is submitted through Ploa, which sends every ready product along with the version anyway). An approved App Store product's changed names or image are a new version of it (ploa_product_get's version.draft), sent the same way while the approved one stays on sale. On Google Play, puts it on sale. ploa_product_get says first what the store still needs under review.missing (listing, price, screenshot, groupName). From an agent this always waits for a person's approval.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_product_review_screenshot
tools.description: Uploads the screenshot App Review looks at for one App Store product (PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB, from an absolute path on this machine): the screen where it's bought in the app. It replaces the one there. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_product_image
tools.description: Uploads the image the App Store shows with one product (where it's promoted, and on its page): PNG or JPEG of exactly 1024×1024 pixels, up to 10 MB, from an absolute path on this machine. It replaces the one there and goes to App Review with the product. While the product is with App Review, Ploa keeps the image and sends it itself once Apple has decided (the answer says so; nothing to retry). App Store only: Google Play keeps no image for a product. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_offers_get
tools.description: A subscription's offers as its store has them, each with its id, type, state (active, draft, scheduled, inactive, ended) and terms. App Store types: intro (the introductory offer, one per country, read as one: the free trial is one too), promotional (code is what the app signs), winback (who it's for under winback), code (offer codes; customers and how many codes were made). Google Play: offers on the base plan, with phases ({ duration, periods, kind: free | discount | price, percent, price }), eligibility (new_app, new_subscription, upgrade, developer), upgradeFrom and tags; trial is true for the free trial the product sets. Prices are US dollars. A Google Play productId is "product:basePlan".

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_offer_save
tools.description: Creates an offer on one subscription (leave offerId out), or changes or ends one (offerId from ploa_offers_get), straight to the store (needs a token allowed to submit). End one with values { state: "ended" }; put a Google Play draft or ended offer on sale with { state: "active" }. App Store values: type (intro, promotional, winback, code), mode (free, pay_as_you_go, pay_up_front), duration (P3D P1W P2W P1M P2M P3M P6M P1Y; for pay_as_you_go the length of each period), periods (pay_as_you_go: 1 to 12), price (US dollars such as "0.99": Apple picks its nearest price point at or above and the equal price in every country); promotional: name and code (what the app signs); winback: name, code (its offer ID), paidMonths, sinceMonths [min, max], startDate (YYYY-MM-DD), optional endDate, waitMonths, priority (high, normal); code: name, customers (new, existing, expired), stackWithIntro. A new intro replaces the one there, the free trial too, country by country: it answers with a job that ploa_product_job follows (offerId "intro" changes or ends it). Only a promotional offer's price and a win-back's dates, priority and months change later; offer codes only end. Google Play values: code (the offer ID: lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens), phases (one or two: [{ duration such as P7D or P1M, periods, kind: free | discount | price, percent (1-99) or price }]; Play allows one paid phase, so two are a free one then a paid one), eligibility (new_app, new_subscription, upgrade with upgradeFrom another subscription's product ID or empty for another base plan of this one, developer: only when the app asks for it), tags. On a base plan already on sale a new offer goes on sale at once; otherwise with the plan. From an agent, a new offer, a price, phases or putting one on sale wait for a person's approval; ending and the rest go straight through.

offerId.description: The offer to change or end; leave out to create.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_offer_codes
tools.description: The codes of one App Store offer code (offerId "code:…" from ploa_offers_get). action list: its batches of one-time codes and its custom codes, each with an id, count, expiry and whether it still works. action create (values { kind: one_time | custom, count, expires: YYYY-MM-DD, customCode for custom }): one-time codes (up to 25,000 a batch) Apple makes in a few minutes, or one custom code people type (count is how many times it can be redeemed); from an agent this waits for a person's approval. action download (batchId of one-time codes, saveTo an absolute path for the CSV file): writes the codes to that file and says how many; it never prints them. action end (batchId): those codes stop working.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_revenuecat_create_product
tools.description: Creates a product the store already has in the app's RevenueCat project, under the same identifier so purchases unlock what they should, and optionally adds it to an entitlement and to a package of the current offering. values: platform (ios or android), storeId (the store's product ID; a Google Play subscription is "product:basePlan"), kind (subscription, consumable, non_consumable), displayName, entitlementId and packageId (from ploa_revenuecat_product_options). Always waits for a person's approval when an agent asks.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_revenuecat_product_options
tools.description: The RevenueCat project's entitlements and the packages of its current offering, with the IDs ploa_revenuecat_create_product takes.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_sales
tools.description: This app's downloads from each store's daily reports: first-time downloads (Google Play: new users) and updates for the last 30 days, against the 30 days before, with a value per day for 60 days. Also each store page's funnel: App Store impressions, product page views, downloads by source, conversion, sessions and deletions (from Apple's analytics reports, once a person has started them), and Play's store listing visitors and acquisitions by traffic source. For tokens of the workspace's owners, also Apple's proceeds and Google's earnings per currency and RevenueCat's numbers; anyone else's token gets downloads only. A store whose reports can't be read says what to set up (the App Store vendor number and a key role that can read sales, or the Play reports bucket and permission). Reports are daily, so answers are kept for hours.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of using the kept answer.

tools.name: ploa_testflight_get
tools.description: The app's TestFlight as App Store Connect has it: tester groups (internal or external, how many testers, the public link and its limit, which builds each has; an internal group may get every build on its own), the beta information Apple's beta review needs (description and feedback email per language) and the beta review contact (the demo password is never shown, only whether one is set), and what is still missing before a build can go to beta review. With buildId (from ploa_release_status or the store's builds), that build's side too: What to Test per language, the groups that have it, its beta review state and its export compliance answer. With groupId, the group's testers and where each stands (invited, accepted, installed).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_testflight_save
tools.description: One TestFlight change, straight to App Store Connect (needs a token allowed to submit). values by action — group.create: { name, internal (bool), allBuilds (bool, internal groups) }. group.update: { groupId, name, feedback (bool), allBuilds (bool, internal groups: every build on its own), publicLink (bool, external groups), publicLinkLimit (number or null) }. group.delete: { groupId }. testers.add: { groupId, testers: [{ email, firstName, lastName }] }: Apple emails each one, so from an agent it waits for a person's approval. testers.remove: { groupId, testerIds }. build.whatToTest: { buildId, text, locale (default the app's primary language) }. build.groups: { buildId, add: [groupId], remove: [groupId] } (an external group gets a build once beta review approved it). build.encryption: { buildId, usesNonExemptEncryption }. build.submitBeta: { buildId, label }: sends the build to beta review so external testers can have it; from an agent it waits for a person's approval, and it needs the beta information first. info: { locale, description, feedbackEmail, marketingUrl, privacyPolicyUrl }. review: { contactFirstName, contactLastName, contactPhone, contactEmail, demoAccountRequired, demoAccountName, demoAccountPassword, notes }.

values.description: The fields for the action, as described above.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_play_testers_get
tools.description: Google Play's testing tracks as Play has them: internal testing, closed testing (alpha and any closed track of the app's own naming) and open testing, each with the release on it now (name, version codes, status) and, for internal and closed tracks, its tester Google Groups. Play's API knows testers only as Google Groups: Play Console's email lists (the only kind internal testing takes there) aren't in it, and open testing has no list. Also the opt-in link testers join through and the app's Play Console IDs. testersError says why the groups couldn't be read (Play's daily edit limit for the app, mostly). Kept for 10 minutes; fresh asks Play again, which may use one of the app's daily edits.

track.description: Only this track, like internal or alpha.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_play_testers_save
tools.description: Adds and takes out tester Google Groups (by their email address, like testers@googlegroups.com) on one internal or closed testing track, straight to Google Play in one edit (needs a token allowed to submit). Everyone in an added group can then join through the opt-in link and get the track's build, so from an agent it waits for a person's approval. Single email addresses can't be added: Play's API takes only Google Groups; email lists are managed in Play Console. Open testing has no list. Play allows each app only so many edits a day: change several groups in one call rather than one call each.

track.description: The testing track, like internal or alpha (ploa_play_testers_get lists them).

add.description: Google Groups to add, by email address.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_reviews_get
tools.description: Customer reviews of the app from the App Store and Google Play in one list, newest first: stars, title, text, the reviewer's name, the App Store country or the Google Play language, the app version (Google Play only), the date, and the developer's reply if there is one. Each store's ratings summary too (the App Store's own average and count; for Google Play, the average of the reviews read). Google Play gives only reviews with text from about the last week; older ones are only in Play Console. Filter by store, stars (a list such as [1, 2]) and unanswered.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of Ploa's last answer (a few minutes old at most).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_review_reply
tools.description: Replies to a review from ploa_reviews_get (reviewId such as apple:123 or google:abc), in the store, under the review, where anyone can read it. A new reply replaces the one there was. Empty text takes the App Store reply back (Google Play can't). At most 5970 characters on the App Store and 350 on Google Play. Write it as the app's developer: thank, answer the point, no promises the team hasn't made. From an agent it waits for a person's approval (needs a token allowed to submit).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_marketing_get
tools.description: The App Store's custom product pages (each with its state, its own link with ppid, which version is live, and its languages with promotional text) and product page optimization A/B tests (state, share of visitors, start and end, treatments with their alternate icon) of the app. Give pageId or testId for one page's or test's screenshots and previews per language (with the localization IDs ploa_marketing_upload needs). options: true lists the live version's languages and the alternate icons its build carries for tests. Apple's API gives no test results (impressions, conversion, improvement): those are only in App Store Connect › Product Page Optimization. Google Play's custom store listings and store listing experiments have no API: they are made in Play Console.

fresh.description: Ask Apple again instead of Ploa's last answer (a few minutes old at most).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_marketing_save
tools.description: One change to the App Store's custom product pages or A/B tests (needs a token allowed to submit). action and body: page.create { name, template: "listing" (a copy of the live product page, the default) | "blank" (with locale and promotionalText) | "page:<pageId>" }; page.update { pageId, name?, visible? }; page.text { pageId, locale, promotionalText } (170 characters; a new locale adds that language); page.newVersion { pageId } (to change an approved page); page.remove { pageId }; page.review { pageId }; test.create { name, trafficProportion (percent of visitors who see a treatment, 1-100), treatments: [{ name, appIconName? }] (1 to 3; icons from ploa_marketing_get options) }; test.update { testId, name?, trafficProportion? }; test.treatment { testId, treatmentId? (leave out to add), name, appIconName? }; test.treatmentRemove { testId, treatmentId }; test.locale { testId, treatmentId, locale } (then upload its screenshots); test.remove { testId }; test.review { testId }; test.start { testId } (once App Review approved it); test.stop { testId } (it can't start again); media.remove { owner: page|test, parentId, localizationId, kind: screenshot|preview, id }; media.order { owner, parentId, localizationId, kind, setId, ids }. From an agent, page.review, test.review, test.start and test.stop wait for a person's approval; removing a page people saw, or a test that ran, is a person's.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_marketing_upload
tools.description: Uploads one file from an absolute path on this machine to a custom product page's language (owner page, parentId the page ID) or an A/B test treatment's language (owner test, parentId the test ID), by the localizationId ploa_marketing_get shows for the page or test. kind screenshot: PNG or JPEG up to 10 MB, type an App Store display type such as APP_IPHONE_67 or APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129. kind preview: an app preview video (MOV, M4V or MP4; H.264, 15 to 30 seconds, at most 30 fps and 500 MB, in the device size's resolution, checked before anything is sent), type such as IPHONE_67 or IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129, up to 3 per device size. Only while the page's version or the test is being prepared. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_events_get
tools.description: The app's In-App Events on the App Store, soonest first: ID, reference name, badge, state (DRAFT, READY_FOR_REVIEW, WAITING_FOR_REVIEW, IN_REVIEW, REJECTED, ACCEPTED, APPROVED, PUBLISHED, PAST, ARCHIVED), dates per group of territories (UTC), deep link, purchase requirement, priority, purpose, the name and descriptions per language, whether each language has its event card and details page media (and Apple's processing state), and what an editable event still needs before App Review. Also Apple's limits and allowed values. Pass eventId for one event.

fresh.description: Ask Apple again instead of Ploa's last answer (a few minutes old at most).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_event_save
tools.description: Makes a new In-App Event (no eventId: referenceName and badge required) or changes a draft or rejected one (eventId; send only what changes). Nothing reaches people until App Review approves it (ploa_event_submit). Fields: referenceName (≤64, only in App Store Connect), badge (LIVE_EVENT, PREMIERE, CHALLENGE, COMPETITION, NEW_SEASON, MAJOR_UPDATE, SPECIAL_EVENT), deepLink (universal link or the app's URL; null removes), purchaseRequirement (NO_COST_ASSOCIATED, IN_APP_PURCHASE), priority (NORMAL, HIGH), purpose (APPROPRIATE_FOR_ALL_USERS, ATTRACT_NEW_USERS, KEEP_ACTIVE_USERS_INFORMED, BRING_BACK_LAPSED_USERS), primaryLocale, schedules: [{ territories: "all" or ["USA", ...] (Apple's 3-letter codes), publishStart, eventStart, eventEnd }] as ISO dates (at most 31 days long, shown at most 14 days before the start), locales: { "en-US": { name (≤30), shortDescription (≤50), longDescription (≤120) }, "fr-FR": null removes a language }. No prices or "#1" claims in the text (App Review rejects them). Then add media with ploa_event_media_upload. Needs a token allowed to submit.

eventId.description: The event to change; leave out to make a new one.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_event_media_upload
tools.description: Uploads the event card (slot card: 16:9, 1920×1080 to 3840×2160) or details page (slot details: 9:16, 1080×1920 to 2160×3840) media of one language of an event: a PNG or JPEG picture, or a MOV, M4V or MP4 video (30 or 60 fps), from an absolute path on this machine. It replaces the one there was. The language's text must be saved first (ploa_event_save). No text or logos in the media, no borders or gradients: Apple adds those. Needs a token allowed to submit.

path.description: Absolute path to the picture or video.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_event_submit
tools.description: Asks to send a ready event (ploa_events_get says what it still needs) to App Review, in a review submission of its own. Submitting is the owner's decision: from an agent it waits for a person's approval in Ploa (check with ploa_approval_status). Once Apple approves it, the App Store shows it on its dates. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_play_data_safety_send
tools.description: Sends the Data safety answers kept in Ploa to Google Play through its API (Google's own CSV, every question), replacing the whole Data safety form in Play Console; Google then reviews it. Only for an agent its owner made autonomous (see ploa_access): otherwise a person presses Send to Google Play on the store setup page, and this says so. Save the answers with ploa_privacy_save first.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_changes_get
tools.description: Every draft on the store setup, by store: the setup parts (App Store app information, age rating, price, release, App Review; Google Play's contact details) and the store listing per language, field by field. People and agents fill these; ploa_details_send takes them to the stores. Also the changes Ploa keeps while Apple has what they're for with App Review (a product's image, screenshots, text, an event…): Ploa sends those by itself once Apple has decided, so there's nothing to do about them but wait (or have a person discard one).

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_listing_get
tools.description: The store listing (name, subtitle, descriptions, keywords, links, screenshots, App Store app previews with their processing state, Google Play's promo video) of both stores, per language: the app's languages with each store's code (Hebrew is he at Apple and iw-IL at Google), what each store is still missing per language, and for one language every field's live value, draft and character limit, and its screenshots and app previews in their order, each with the id ploa_screenshot_remove and ploa_preview_remove take and its set's setId for ploa_screenshot_order and ploa_preview_order. Videos are optional in both stores. Languages a store doesn't have yet can be added by writing drafts in that store's code and publishing.

language.description: A language code (he, en-US, ja…); without it, the list of languages and what's missing.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_listing_start_version
tools.description: Apple takes text and screenshot changes only on a version being prepared. This creates the next one (e.g. 1.2.0), copying the last version's text and screenshots. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_upload
tools.description: Uploads one image (PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB, from an absolute path on this machine) straight to the store listing. apple types: APP_IPHONE_67 (6.9-inch iPhone, required), APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129 (13-inch iPad), and Apple's other display types; only on a version being prepared. google types: phoneScreenshots (2 to 8), sevenInchScreenshots, tenInchScreenshots, featureGraphic (1024×500, one). The file is checked against the store's rules first (ploa_screenshot_specs, ploa_screenshot_check) and refused with the reasons if the store wouldn't take it. Screenshots go after the ones already in the set: upload in the order they should appear. After an upload that failed (a 502, a timeout), read ploa_listing_get before trying again, since the first one may have arrived; fix the order with ploa_screenshot_order (App Store). Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_remove
tools.description: Removes one screenshot or graphic from the store listing, by the id ploa_listing_get shows. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_order
tools.description: Sets the order of one App Store screenshot set (one language and device size): setId and every screenshot id of the set, each once, in the order they should appear, from ploa_listing_get with that language. Only on a version being prepared. Google Play keeps images in the order they were uploaded: there, remove them and upload again in order. Needs a token allowed to submit.

ids.description: Every screenshot id of the set, first to last.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_preview_upload
tools.description: Optional: the App Store doesn't require app previews, so make one only when the person wants it (ask). Uploads one app preview video (from an absolute path on this machine) to the App Store version being prepared, for one language and device size. Apple's rules, checked before anything is sent: .mov, .m4v or .mp4, H.264 (or ProRes 422 HQ in a .mov), 15 to 30 seconds, at most 30 fps and 500 MB, at most 3 per device size and language, and the device size's resolution (IPHONE_67/65/61/58: 886×1920 or 1920×886; IPHONE_55/40: 1080×1920; IPHONE_47: 750×1334; IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129/3GEN_11/105: 1200×1600; IPAD_97: 900×1200; DESKTOP, APPLE_TV: 1920×1080). Apple processes the video afterwards; ploa_listing_get shows its state. posterAt: the second shown before it plays (Apple's default is 5). Needs a token allowed to submit.

posterAt.description: Seconds into the video for the poster frame.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_preview_remove
tools.description: Removes one app preview from the App Store version being prepared, by the id ploa_listing_get shows. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_preview_order
tools.description: Sets the order of one app preview set (one language and device size, up to 3): setId and every preview id of the set, each once, first to last, from ploa_listing_get with that language. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_preview_poster
tools.description: Chooses the frame people see before an app preview plays: seconds into the video (like 5.5), or Apple's time code hh:mm:ss:ff. Needs a token allowed to submit.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_approval_status
tools.description: Whether a person approved, rejected or hasn't yet decided a request made with ploa_release_submit_review or ploa_release_promote, and, once approved, what the store said.

tools.name: ploa_app_icon_sync
tools.description: Sends the app's icon from this project (the file the Expo config names: ios.icon, else icon) to Ploa, so the dashboard shows it at once instead of waiting for a build to reach the stores. Ploa shows the project's icon until a store shows a newer one. Other Ploa tools already send a changed icon on the way; use this right after changing it.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_details_get
tools.description: Everything both stores ask for, as one set of answers, the same as the person's Store details wizard on ploa.dev: the languages (each with its App Store and Google Play code), the text per language, the links and contact, category, age rating answers (with every question and its allowed answers), price and countries, App Review's contact and demo account, release, and privacy. Plus problems: what each store would refuse now (FIX) and what's likely a mistake (check), each with the step and language it's in, and what's left for the person to enter by hand in a store's console, with links. Start here; then ploa_details_save, ploa_privacy_save, and ploa_details_send.

step.description: Only one step's answers; all when left out.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of the copy from the last two minutes.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_details_save
tools.description:
Saves answers as drafts in Ploa, one step at a time, for both stores at once (a token allowed to draft is enough; nothing reaches a store until ploa_details_send). Returns what each store would still refuse. step and values:
- text: { languages: { <language code from ploa_details_get, or a new one like "fr-FR">: { name (both stores, 30), subtitle (App Store, 30), shortDescription (Google Play, 80), description (both, 4000), keywords (App Store, 100, commas; Ploa tidies them), promotionalText (App Store, 170, optional), whatsNew (App Store, only for an update) } } } — several languages in one call; ask the person which languages first.
- links: { supportUrl, marketingUrl, privacyPolicyUrl } (https; the same in every App Store language).
- contact: { email (public, Google requires it), phone, website }.
- about: { primaryCategory, secondaryCategory, contentRights: "USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT" | "DOES_NOT_USE_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT", declarations: { newsApp, healthApp, financialFeatures, governmentApp } }.
- rating: { age: { <question>: answer } (every question; Google Play's content rating follows from it), ages: [...] (who it's for: the person's decision) }.
- price: { pricePointId (from ploa_appstore_price_points; the person's decision), everywhere: true | false, territories: ["ISR", …], sells: true | false } — an agent's price change waits for a person's approval when sent.
- review: { contactFirstName, contactLastName, contactEmail, contactPhone (+country code), demoAccountRequired, demoAccountName, demoAccountPassword, notes, copyright, releaseType: "AFTER_APPROVAL" | "MANUAL" } — App Review's contact is private and never the store page's.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_privacy_save
tools.description: What the app collects, once for both stores: Apple's App Privacy and Google Play's Data safety are made from it. Read the app's code first (ploa_privacy_hints). apple: { collects: true|false, types: { <type>: { purposes: [appFunctionality|analytics|personalization|developerAdvertising|thirdPartyAdvertising|other], linked: bool, tracking: bool } } } with types name, email, phone, address, otherContact, health, fitness, payment, credit, otherFinancial, preciseLocation, coarseLocation, sensitiveInfo, contacts, emails, photos, audio, gameplay, support, otherContent, browsingHistory, searchHistory, userId, deviceId, purchaseHistory, productInteraction, advertisingData, otherUsage, crashData, performanceData, otherDiagnostic, environmentScanning, hands, head, otherData. google: { encryptedInTransit, deletionRequest, accountCreation: [usernamePassword|usernameOtherAuth|usernamePasswordOtherAuth|oauth|other] or ["none"], accountCreationOther, accountDeletionUrl (required with accounts) }. Kept in Ploa: Data safety goes to Google with ploa_play_data_safety_send (or the person's Send); App Privacy is entered by the person in App Store Connect.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_details_send
tools.description: Checks every answer against both stores' rules and, when nothing would be refused, sends every draft to App Store Connect and Google Play in one go, saying per part what each took. When something would be refused, nothing is sent and the problems come back with the step to fix each in. Apple keeps what's for a version with App Review (Ploa sends it once Apple decides); an agent's price change becomes an approval. Needs a token allowed to submit; otherwise tell the person to press Send on the Store details page.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_specs
tools.description: The stores' screenshot rules per device type, from Apple's and Google's own pages: the exact sizes (Apple) or the range (Google Play), how many a set holds, the format, the size to make, which sets each store asks for, and a simulator that captures each Apple size as is. Then, for the app in this folder, what its store page has per language and which screenshot sets it still needs. Also the videos the page has, which are optional (App Store app previews, Google Play's promo video): ask the person before making one. Start here before making screenshots; capture them with ploa_screenshot_capture, check them with ploa_screenshot_check, and upload with ploa_screenshot_upload.

store.description: One store; both when left out.

all.description: Apple's older devices, Mac, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Watch too.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_check
tools.description: Checks image files on this machine (absolute paths) against a store's rules, from each file's own header: PNG or JPEG, no transparency, the size (Apple: exactly one of the device size's; Google Play: 320 to 3840 px a side, at most twice as long as wide; the feature graphic exactly 1024×500) and the file size. With type, against that device type, and says if there are more files than a set holds; without it, which of the store's types take each file as it is. Nothing is sent anywhere.

type.description: Apple's display type (APP_IPHONE_67, APP_IPAD_PRO_3GEN_129…) or Google Play's image type (phoneScreenshots, sevenInchScreenshots, tenInchScreenshots, featureGraphic).

tools.name: ploa_screenshot_capture
tools.description: Saves what a booted iOS Simulator (xcrun simctl) or Android emulator or device (adb screencap) shows now, as a PNG, and says which of the store's types take it as it is. It only captures: run the app and bring it to the screen first; nothing is installed, booted or launched. Saved under the app's store/screenshots/<platform>/ unless folder says otherwise; an alpha channel is removed, since the stores refuse transparency. Pick the device by name or ID when several are running; list: true only lists them. For Apple's sizes, capture on the simulator ploa_screenshot_specs names (an iPhone 17 Pro Max gives the 6.9-inch 1320×2868).

platform.description: Needed only when both an iOS Simulator and an Android device are running.

device.description: The simulator's name or UDID, or the Android device's serial or model.

list.description: Only list the running simulators and devices.

name.description: The file's name, like 01-home.png. Defaults to the device and the time.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_privacy_hints
tools.description: Reads this app's package.json, Expo config, Info.plist purpose strings, AndroidManifest permissions, the privacy manifests of the app and its SDKs, and its imports, and returns hints for Apple's App Privacy and Google Play's Data safety: each well-known SDK (analytics, crash reporting, ads, push, sign-in, payments…) and permission with the data types and purposes it usually involves, in the keys ploa_privacy_save takes. Each hint says where it was found, whether it collects by design or only depending on how the app uses it, and what to check in the code. Also flags tracking (ATT, the advertising ID), sharing with third parties, ads, account deletion when there is sign-in, and encryption in transit. Local and deterministic; it doesn't decide the answers.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

tools.name: ploa_review_rejection
tools.description: Everything the App Store and Google Play said when they turned something down, in one place: the App Store version (REJECTED, METADATA_REJECTED, INVALID_BINARY), builds Apple's processing refused, TestFlight beta review, in-app purchases and subscriptions, in-app events, custom product pages and tests, Google Play releases its review didn't approve, and releases or approved requests the store refused on the way. Each with its state, when, every reason the stores' APIs give, the message the person pasted from App Store Connect or Play Console with its guideline numbers and ITMS codes, the link where the full text is, and what to do next. Apple's API has no App Review message or guideline numbers, and Google's none for policy rejections: when the person gives you that text, pass it as text (with item, the rejection's key from this tool, or store) and Ploa keeps it with the rejection, in the audit log. Start here when an app was rejected.

text.description: The store's message as the person copied it (App Store Connect › App Review, or Play Console's Inbox), to keep in Ploa. Up to 20000 characters.

item.description: Which rejection the text belongs to: its key from this tool (like apple:version:…). Leave out for the store's newest.

store.description: With text and no item: whose message it is.

fresh.description: Ask the stores again instead of the answer from the last ten minutes.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

instructions:
Ploa takes this app to the App Store and Google Play.
A new app, or a store or Ploa not set up yet: start with ploa_setup_guide. It says what's left, in order, who does each step (the person or you) and the links, and suggests the app's ID (bundle ID and package name) when there's none. Pass the person their steps one store at a time, in their language and with the links; do yours (ploa_link, ploa_appstore_register_bundle_id); run the guide again after each.
Ask, don't assume: the store page's languages, the countries the app is in, its price, who it's for, App Review's contact (private) and the store page's contact (public) are the person's decisions; one given for the first is never used for the second. Ask them (ploa_setup_guide lists the questions with what the code suggests) and wait for the answers before saving any of it.
Keep the person oriented: at the start of the work show them the stages board from ploa_setup_guide, and after every step show it again with what was just done (and by whom: you, them or Ploa), what's left, what's needed from them, and what Ploa updates in the stores by itself.
Say plainly what Ploa can't update: Apple's App Privacy and Play Console's App content forms other than Data safety are entered by the person in the store's console (Apple has no API for keys or for creating the app either; the guide says what to do). For each, tell them what to enter and where (ploa_details_get lists each with its answers and link; the Store details page's Privacy step has them too), and that they tick it there once done.
Every instruction for the person comes from ploa_setup_guide: a certificate, a capability to turn on at Apple, a console form, a key. When a tool's error asks something of the person, run the guide and pass on its step rather than your own wording. Give every link as a clickable markdown link, [name](https://…), as the guide writes them; never an address or a path to type.
Usual order once set up: ploa_preflight (fix what it finds), then ploa_release_start, then ploa_release_status until the build is on TestFlight or internal testing.
App Review and production need a person: ploa_release_submit_review (replace: true sends a newer build in place of the one with App Review), ploa_release_withdraw_review and ploa_release_promote only ask, and ploa_approval_status tells you the answer. Wait for it; never try another way around an approval. If the person made this agent autonomous (ploa_access says so), the same tools carry it out at once instead, approved in advance, and everything is still recorded under the agent's name.
To see where everything stands (builds, submissions, the last run): ploa_shipping_report. ploa_runs shows each release step by step.
The store details (text, screenshots, category, age rating, price, App Review's contact, privacy) are yours to write: Ploa has no AI of its own. They're one set of answers for both stores: start from ploa_details_get, read the app's code to know what it does, save with ploa_details_save (many languages at once) and ploa_privacy_save, and fix what each store would refuse. A person checks and sends it all with one click on ploa.dev; send yourself (ploa_details_send) only if ploa_access says you're autonomous. Videos (App Store app previews, Google Play's promo video) are optional, never required: ask the person whether they want one before making it.
While Apple has something with App Review (the app's version, a product, an event), a change to it (an image, screenshots, text) is kept in Ploa and sent by Ploa once Apple has decided: the tool says "Kept in Ploa". That's done as far as you're concerned; don't retry it or look for another way. ploa_changes_get lists what's kept.
Step-by-step briefs are this server's prompts: set_up_app, fill_store_page, translate_store_page, make_screenshots, answer_privacy, handle_rejection, write_release_notes.
